players.product: batch / single-wafer wet cleaning systems (incl. HBM TSV cleaning) and transfer robots

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: H1 2026 consolidated revenue KRW 137,282M, down 30.57% from KRW 197,728M in H1 2025, with an operating loss of KRW 26,774M (H1 2025 operating profit KRW 277M) and a net loss of KRW 12,640M. Q2 alone: revenue KRW 82,392M (Q2 2025 KRW 116,164M) and an operating loss of KRW 9,635M (Q2 2025 operating profit KRW 672M). Product sales fell 36.68% to KRW 76,011M; the equipment segment posted an operating loss of KRW 25,300M. Japanese subsidiary J.E.T. (66.28% owned, batch cleaning) had H1 revenue KRW 54,821,066 thousand and a net loss of KRW 10,772,765 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue KRW 137,282M (-30.57%); H1 operating loss KRW 26,774M; Q2 revenue KRW 82,392M; Q2 operating loss KRW 9,635M

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 revenue by product: semiconductor cleaning equipment (ATOM, APOLLON, VENUS) KRW 84,060M (61.23%), industrial robots and vacuum KRW 35,362M (25.76%), display equipment (HELIA) KRW 10,628M (7.74%), plug valves KRW 7,232M (5.27%). Consolidated revenue by location before eliminations: Korea KRW 70,296,313 thousand, Japan, China and others KRW 81,370,482 thousand. The largest single customer (unnamed, customer A) accounted for KRW 22,805,965 thousand of consolidated revenue (H1 2025: KRW 41,211,633 thousand).
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor equipment KRW 84,060M (61.23%); robots KRW 35,362M (25.76%); display KRW 10,628M (7.74%); customer A KRW 22,805,965 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog at 2026-06-30 of KRW 376,334M out of total orders of KRW 513,616M: special-purpose manufacturing equipment (equipment segment) KRW 276,040M for delivery between 2026-01-01 and 2027-12-31, plug valves KRW 11,204M, other (merchandise etc.) KRW 89,090M. Contract liabilities (customer advances) rose to KRW 55,372,026 thousand from KRW 29,071,667 thousand at end-2025.
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog KRW 376,334M; equipment backlog KRW 276,040M; contract liabilities KRW 55,372,026 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex: production is build-to-order, so the company reports manufacturing cost as capacity; semiconductor equipment output was KRW 73,546M in H1 2026 (full-year 2025: KRW 119,848M). A new plant site in the Yongin semiconductor cluster is under way: land contract KRW 14,118M (2024-07 to 2027-12), KRW 9,883M paid; construction in progress rose to KRW 23,805M. The company says its integrated site is complete, letting it push localization and volume production of batch-type cleaning tools alongside single-wafer tools. Inventory KRW 160,441M, of which work in process KRW 56,128M.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor equipment output KRW 73,546M; Yongin land KRW 14,118M (KRW 9,883M paid); construction in progress KRW 23,805M

quarterly_data.signal: HBM-related products in the report: Ring Frame cleaning equipment used in next-generation packaging for HBM production (de-bonding the device wafer from the carrier, residue cleaning and chip cutting on ultra-thin wafers), commercialised for 300mm and 400mm cleaning tools (product ATOM); the company expects continued benefit from HBM market growth. It has developed Temporary Bonding / De-bonding (TBDB) equipment for HBM chip stacking and bumping, offering mechanical, laser and photonic debond (the photonic method has no mass-production record yet), under government projects for HBM ultra-thin wafer bonding and debonding (2022.04 to 2025.12) and a UV laser debonding system for 2.5D packaging (2024.04 to 2026.12); these tools are currently dependent on foreign suppliers and Zeus aims to localise them. Also developing PEP (Pressurized Etch Process) wet etch equipment and a 12-chamber ION 12 cleaner (more than twice the throughput of 8-chamber tools). R&D spend KRW 23,290,765 thousand in H1 2026 (17.0% of revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: R&D KRW 23,290,765 thousand (17.0% of revenue); Ring Frame for 300mm and 400mm; ION 12: 12 chambers

quarterly_data.signal: Management (business overview): customers are expanding capacity through active facility investment driven by AI, and Zeus will keep expanding its main cleaning tools (ATOM, ION-12, APOLLON, BW series, high-temperature sulfuric acid tool) while stabilising equipment and responding to next-generation processes; the company expects demand for HBM and PIM to support the equipment market and says cleaning becomes more important as processes get finer and more complex.
